name: North Miami Beach
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in North Miami Beach, FL 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in North Miami Beach, FL: Snow Fest, Elves and Oars at Oleta River, the Grinch and Santa, library letters to Santa.
lede: North Miami Beach celebrates with a city Snow Fest and holiday parade at City Hall, a Letters to Santa night at its Discovery Library and a movie night by a bonfire on the Oleta River.
celebrates: The City of North Miami Beach holds its Snow Fest and Holiday Parade each December at City Hall, 17011 NE 19th Avenue, with rides, food, festive music and entertainment for all ages, plus a tree lighting. The Discovery Library at 1601 NE 164th Street has hosted a Letters to Santa evening with story time, letter writing, a visit with Santa, a gift raffle, snacks and crafts. At Oleta River State Park, 3400 NE 163rd Street, Oleta River Adventures runs a holiday paddle and movie night, and Bella Christmas Trees on Biscayne Boulevard has hosted free Grinch and Santa evenings.
lastyear: The City of North Miami Beach's calendar listed its Snow Fest and Holiday Parade for Saturday, December 13, 2025, from 5 to 10 pm at City Hall, with thrilling rides, food, festive music and entertainment for all ages. The calendar also listed Letters to Santa for Friday, December 12, 2025, at 6 pm at the Discovery Library, with story time, letters to Santa, a visit with Santa, a gift raffle, snacks and crafts. Both listings were posted in advance.
facts: North Miami Beach began as a settlement platted in 1881 called Fulford by the Sea. It was incorporated in 1926 as the Town of Fulford, named for Captain William H. Fulford of the Coast Guard, and became the City of North Miami Beach in 1931. Carl Fisher built a wooden racetrack there with stands for 12,000 spectators, the Fulford Miami Speedway, and the 1926 hurricane destroyed it after one race. The city's motto is Where People Care.
trains: For trains near North Miami Beach, Brightline's Aventura station is at 19796 West Dixie Highway and its MiamiCentral station is at 161 NW 6th Street in Miami. Metrorail's Green Line runs between Palmetto and Dadeland South, and Tri-Rail's Miami Airport station is at 3861 NW 21st Street. Tri-Rail riders headed to MiamiCentral transfer at the Metrorail Transfer Station. For a bigger train day, the Gold Coast Railroad Museum in Miami has its own page on our site.

traditions: The city's annual holiday celebration at City Hall, with rides, food, music and a tree lighting.
A Discovery Library evening with story time, letters, Santa, snacks and a gift raffle.
A kayak, bonfire and outdoor Elf movie night at Oleta River State Park.

The city's calendar also lists its own menorah lighting each December.
kidfact: North Miami Beach was first called Fulford by the Sea, after a Coast Guard captain. It once had a wooden race track that lasted for one race before a hurricane knocked it down.
faq: Where is North Miami Beach Snow Fest?

Snow Fest is held at North Miami Beach City Hall, 17011 NE 19th Avenue. The city's calendar describes rides, food, festive music and entertainment for all ages, and the 2026 listing mentions a tree lighting and parade. The tourism listing for the event states free admission, and the city's Parks and Recreation Department answers questions at 305-948-2957.
Can kids write letters to Santa in North Miami Beach?

The city's Discovery Library has hosted a Letters to Santa evening. Children enjoy story time, write their own letters, meet Santa and can win prizes in a gift raffle, with snacks and crafts. Call the library at 305-948-2970 to ask whether the program returns this year.
Can families paddle at Oleta River State Park at Christmas?

Oleta River Adventures runs Elves and Oars, a holiday evening that combines a kayak rental with kids winter crafts, hot cocoa, popcorn, a bonfire and an outdoor Elf movie. Its tickets are priced separately for adults and youth, and the host invites guests to wear ugly sweaters or elf outfits.
Why is it called North Miami Beach if it has no beach?

The settlement was first named Fulford by the Sea. The city's boundaries once stretched to the Atlantic Ocean, and it took the name North Miami Beach in 1931. Today the city has no beaches within its limits.
